ov: A stocky, shaggy goat-antelope of the eastern Himalayas, closest to sheep despite its muskox-like looks. Both sexes have thick, upturned horns. It moves between high summer pastures, where herds of up to 300 gather, and lower forests in winter.
rg: The eastern Himalayas in Bhutan and Arunachal Pradesh in India; related takins in China.
df: Leaves and grasses, bamboo shoots and flowers, plus salt from mineral licks.
fx: It can stand on its hind legs to reach leaves more than 3 m up.
When disturbed it gives a cough-like alarm call, and the herd hides by lying down in bamboo thickets.
